problem: Standard LLM alignment relies solely on pairwise preference comparisons, missing richer feedback signals like multiwise rankings that humans naturally provide.
approach: Ranked Choice Preference Optimization (RCPO) unifies preference optimization with choice modeling via maximum likelihood estimation, supporting both utility-based and rank-based models to handle richer feedback formats.
contribution: RCPO subsumes pairwise methods as special cases and demonstrates consistent improvements over baselines on Llama-3, Gemma-2, and Mistral when leveraging ranked preference data.

problem: Existing watermarking methods require decoder access, limiting applicability in real-world scenarios like academic peer review where organizers cannot access the LLM used.
approach: In-Context Watermarking (ICW) embeds watermarks purely through prompt engineering, leveraging LLMs' in-context learning and instruction-following without model access.
contribution: ICW demonstrates feasibility as a model-agnostic, practical watermarking approach, and findings suggest it becomes more viable as LLMs improve.

problem: Identifying whether a suspect LLM is trained from scratch or derived from a base model is difficult when intensive post-training (fine-tuning, pruning, etc.) obscures lineage.
approach: A training-free fingerprinting method leverages weight matrices, Linear Assignment Problem, and centered kernel alignment (CKA) to robustly measure model similarity across post-training transformations.
contribution: Achieves perfect classification on 150 model pairs (60 positive, 90 negative) with near-zero false positives and 30s computation time on GPU.

problem: Self-rewarding methods for LLM reasoning suffer from training collapse due to single-view supervision signals, which create self-consistent illusions and reward hacking.
approach: Co-rewarding introduces complementary supervision from multiple views: contrastive agreement across analogous questions and pseudo-labels via a reference teacher, increasing difficulty of trivial solutions.
contribution: Achieves +3.31% average improvement on mathematical reasoning benchmarks with stable training across setups, especially +7% on specific benchmarks.

problem: Existing precipitation nowcasting models are either computationally expensive or biased toward normal rainfall, and benchmark datasets are skewed, hindering real-world applicability.
approach: exPreCast combines local spatiotemporal attention, texture-preserving cubic dual upsampling, and temporal extractors in a deterministic framework, trained on a balanced radar dataset from Korea Meteorological Administration.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on SEVIR, MeteoNet, and the new balanced KMA dataset with accurate, real-time nowcasts across ordinary and extreme precipitation.

problem: Existing model-free RL algorithms have coarse gap-dependent regret bounds that fail to capture the structure of suboptimality gaps in tabular settings.
approach: Develops a novel analytical framework that explicitly separates analysis of optimal and suboptimal state-action pairs, introduced ULCB-Hoeffding (UCB-based) and refined AMB (non-UCB) with corrected Q-updates and martingale analysis.
contribution: Establishes the first fine-grained gap-dependent regret upper bounds for both UCB and non-UCB methods, with empirical performance improvements.

problem: Current website-generation agents lack comprehensive visual and interaction feedback, relying only on code execution, which fails to capture actual generated code quality.
approach: WebGen-Agent leverages multi-level visual feedback (screenshots, GUI testing, VLM descriptions and scores) with a backtracking mechanism, integrated with Step-GRPO for dense reward signals.
contribution: Increases Claude 3.5 Sonnet's accuracy from 26.4% to 51.9% on WebGen-Bench with improved appearance scores, outperforming state-of-the-art agents.

problem: Out-of-distribution detection for text currently relies on simple average pooling of token embeddings, missing fine-grained token-level information.
approach: AP-OOD exploits token-level information and flexibly interpolates between unsupervised and supervised settings, using semi-supervised learning with limited auxiliary outlier data.
contribution: Reduces FPR95 from 27.77% to 5.91% on XSUM and from 75.19% to 68.13% on WMT15 En-Fr, setting state-of-the-art OOD detection for text.

problem: Bidirectional language models demonstrate stronger context understanding than unidirectional ones, but the theoretical reason is unclear.
approach: FlowNIB analyzes bidirectional vs. unidirectional models through information bottleneck theory, introducing a post-hoc framework to estimate mutual information values per layer.
contribution: Demonstrates that bidirectional LM layers retain higher mutual information than similar-sized unidirectional LMs, explaining superior performance on NLU and reasoning tasks.

problem: Generalization error of minimum-norm solutions in overparameterized regression is not fully characterized, especially how spike strength and target-spike alignment interact.
approach: Analyzes spiked covariance data models through exact generalization error expressions, classifying benign, tempered, and catastrophic overfitting regimes based on spike strength and aspect ratio.
contribution: Shows that increasing spike strength can surprisingly induce catastrophic overfitting before achieving benign overfitting, and identifies when target-spike alignment is detrimental.

problem: Training reasoning models with latent reasoning traces is unstable, and the connection between variational inference and RL-style methods for reasoning is unclear.
approach: Variational reasoning treats thinking traces as latent variables, extends ELBO to multi-trace objectives with forward-KL formulation, and interprets rejection sampling and GRPO as local forward-KL objectives.
contribution: Provides principled probabilistic perspective unifying variational inference with RL methods, achieving stable training with improved reasoning on Qwen 2.5 and 3 across diverse tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle in abstract visual reasoning tasks, and whether the bottleneck is reasoning or perception remains unclear.
approach: Introduces VisuRiddles benchmark and synthesizer to systematically evaluate fine-grained perception, and proposes PAVR (Perception-Augmented Visual Reasoner) with two-stage training for perception then reasoning.
contribution: PAVR substantially outperforms open-source and commercial MLLMs, demonstrating fine-grained perception as the primary bottleneck in abstract visual reasoning.

problem: Robotic manipulation requires jointly learning visual representations and action policies, with limited supervision for diverse embodiments.
approach: Genie Envisioner (GE) combines an instruction-conditioned video diffusion model (GE-Base) for learning spatial-temporal dynamics with a lightweight flow-matching decoder (GE-Act) for policy inference.
contribution: Trained on over 1 million episodes, GE supports both short- and long-horizon tasks with generalization across embodiments without finetuning.

problem: It is unknown whether open-ended reading goals can be automatically decoded from eye movements alone, a task never previously studied.
approach: Develops goal decoding tasks and multimodal text-eye-movement LLMs for both discriminative selection and generative reconstruction of reader goals.
contribution: Demonstrates considerable success in goal selection among options and progress toward free-form textual goal reconstruction, opening new avenues for goal-driven reading research.

problem: Agent evaluation frameworks lack scalability across domains and do not systematically account for user expertise and conversation quality.
approach: TED framework combines reusable user personas (expert/non-expert), natural language grading notes for subgoals, and automated error analysis to diagnose agent failures.
contribution: Reveals insights on agent performance across models and user expertise levels, providing actionable feedback for improvement.

problem: View synthesis requires explicit 3D representations or single-image references, limiting practical applicability and generalization.
approach: Kaleido treats 3D as a specialized video subdomain, using masked autoregressive sequence-to-sequence generation on a rectified flow transformer to unify 3D and video within one decoder.
contribution: Sets state-of-the-art on view synthesis benchmarks, matching per-scene optimization in many-view settings and substantially outperforming in few-view zero-shot settings.

problem: Existing mesh reconstruction methods entangle geometry and texture, allowing textures to mask geometric errors and creating ambiguous multi-modal solutions.
approach: DiMeR disentangles geometry from texture using normal maps as strict geometry indicators (separate from RGB), streamlines extraction, and adds 3D supervision via EM-style prototype updates.
contribution: Generalizes across sparse-view, single-image, and text-to-3D tasks with 30%+ Chamfer Distance reduction on GSO and OmniObject3D datasets.

problem: Video diffusion transformers fail to generalize beyond training length, exhibiting periodic content repetition and quality degradation during extrapolation.
approach: UltraViCo suppresses attention for tokens beyond the training window via constant decay, addressing attention dispersion as the unified cause of both failure modes.
contribution: Pushes extrapolation from ~2× to 4× length, improving Dynamic Degree and Imaging Quality by 233% and 40.5% at 4× extrapolation.

problem: Evaluating LLM code generation relies on manual annotations and focuses primarily on Python, missing difficulty diversity and multilingual coverage.
approach: AutoCodeGen constructs multilingual datasets via LLM test generation, sandbox execution, reverse generation, and multi-stage filtering without manual annotation.
contribution: AutoCodeBench spans 20 languages with balanced coverage and high difficulty, revealing that state-of-the-art models struggle especially in low-resource languages.

problem: Time series anomaly detection relies on unimodal numerical data, overlooking complementary information from text and semantic relationships.
approach: MindTS integrates exogenous and endogenous text through cross-view fusion and multimodal alignment, using content condenser to filter redundancy and enable cross-modal reconstruction.
contribution: Achieves competitive or superior results on six real-world multimodal datasets through semantic alignment and condensed interaction.

problem: LLMs frequently fail to recognize false presuppositions in real patient cancer questions, posing safety risks in medical decision-making.
approach: Introduces Cancer-Myth benchmark of expert-verified questions with false presuppositions and studies mitigation via precautionary prompts and GEPA optimization.
contribution: No frontier LLM corrects false presuppositions more than 43% of the time, though GEPA raises accuracy to 80% at the cost of 41% misidentification on presupposition-free questions.

problem: Generating complete neural network weights is limited to partial or small models due to high-dimensional symmetries and computational demands.
approach: DeepWeightFlow uses flow matching in weight space with Git Re-Basin canonicalization to handle permutation symmetries, enabling efficient generation of diverse full-sized networks.
contribution: Generates ensembles of hundreds of networks in minutes without finetuning, scaling to large architectures with better transfer learning performance than diffusion methods.

problem: Classifier-Free Guidance's impact on sampling dynamics in diffusion models, especially under multimodal conditionals, remains poorly understood.
approach: Analyzes CFG through three successive stages: Direction Shift (initialization bias), Mode Separation (diversity suppression), and Concentration (fine-grained variability reduction).
contribution: Explains guidance-quality/diversity tradeoff and proposes time-varying guidance schedules that improve both quality and diversity.

problem: NLP models often replicate social bias, yet input-based explanations' role in detecting and mitigating bias for fairness remains unclear and largely unquantified.
approach: Conducts systematic quantitative study of explainability-fairness relationship in hate speech detection across encoder and decoder models, examining bias detection, model selection, and mitigation.
contribution: Shows explanations effectively detect biased predictions and supervise training but unreliably select fair models, bridging explainability and fairness in NLP.

problem: Existing open-source visual captioning models significantly lag behind commercial ones, limiting applications like data synthesis.
approach: CapFlow uses multi-agent collaboration to synthesize high-quality captions from open-source models, then fine-tunes on this data to create MetaCaptioner, a generalist captioner.
contribution: Achieves GPT-4.1-level caption quality across domains with 89.5% cost reduction, matching commercial performance while maintaining open-source availability.

problem: LLMs lack awareness of author intents that guide report generation, limiting quality of knowledge-intensive long-form outputs.
approach: Uses structured tag-based schemes to elicit implicit authorial intents, then leverages extracted intents to improve zero-shot generation and create synthetic fine-tuning data.
contribution: Improves performance by +2.9 points for large models and +12.3 points for small models on scientific report generation tasks, with enhanced citation usage and readability.

problem: Complex multimodal policies for LLM-based agents are unwieldy in-context, imposing large computational costs while models struggle to faithfully follow them.
approach: Multimodal Policy Internalization (MPI) internalizes reasoning-intensive multimodal policies into model parameters via fine-tuning, eliminating need for in-context policies.
contribution: Enables stronger policy-following without in-context policies, addressing data and algorithmic challenges of multimodal policy internalization.

problem: MLLMs' ability to understand immersive omnidirectional environments (360° views) is unexplored, yet relevant for VR/AR and embodied AI.
approach: Introduces ODI-Bench with 2,000 high-quality omnidirectional images and 4,000+ QA pairs across 10 tasks, benchmarking 20 MLLMs and proposing Omni-CoT for enhanced reasoning.
contribution: Shows current MLLMs struggle with omnidirectional context, while Omni-CoT training-free method significantly enhances comprehension through chain-of-thought.

problem: SVD-based model merging methods rely on heuristic rank selection, leading to inter-task interference and suboptimal multi-task performance.
approach: AdaRank adaptively selects singular components per layer via entropy minimization on unlabeled test data, replacing fixed heuristic ranks with data-driven adaptation.
contribution: Consistently improves merging across diverse backbones and modalities, narrowing performance gap against individually fine-tuned models.

problem: Reference-based image generation is limited to single-image references and cannot leverage 3D assets for spatial consistency.
approach: RefAny3D uses dual-branch perception with multi-view RGB and point maps of 3D assets, with domain-decoupled generation ensuring spatially aligned but content-disentangled outputs.
contribution: Effectively uses 3D assets as references for image generation with consistency, opening new possibilities for combining diffusion with 3D content creation.

problem: Prototypical self-supervised learning suffers from partial prototype collapse, where multiple prototypes converge to identical representations, undermining diversity.
approach: Introduces fully decoupled training separating encoder and prototype optimization, modeling prototypes as a Gaussian mixture updated via online EM independent of encoder loss.
contribution: Eliminates prototype collapse without explicit regularization, yielding consistently diverse prototypes that translate to improved downstream performance.

problem: Finetuned LLM-judges' real-world deployment concerns are ignored, including generalization to future/past models and unseen questions.
approach: Studies three shelf-life aspects—future-proofing, backward-compatibility, and question generalization—across reasoning datasets with varying train-test distributions and multiple fine-tuning algorithms.
contribution: Shows future-proofing is challenging while backward-compatibility is easier; DPO-trained models improve backward-compatibility; continual learning better balances adaptation.

problem: Selecting training data for fine-tuning is challenging when only few target-distribution samples exist, and existing methods treat them as validation.
approach: Train on Validation (ToV) inverts the usual split: performs inference on training pool before and after fine-tuning on validation set, selecting samples whose predictions change most.
contribution: Achieves lower test log-loss than state-of-the-art data selection approaches on instruction tuning and NER, with theoretical analysis supporting the method.

problem: VLMs struggle with spatial reasoning in realistic, unconstrained contexts, yet prior work relied on synthetic or puzzle-like setups.
approach: Introduces SpatiaLab with 1,400 QA pairs across six categories and 30 task types covering relative positioning, depth, orientation, size, navigation, and 3D geometry.
contribution: Reveals substantial gaps in spatial reasoning: InternVL3.5-72B achieves 54.93% vs 87.57% human accuracy, showing key limitations in complex spatial understanding.

problem: Transformers' reasoning ability scales with inference-time compute via thinking tokens, but memory constraints and information bottleneck effects limit generalization.
approach: Bottlenecked Transformers performs memory consolidation via periodic KV cache rewrites, theoretically justified by Information Bottleneck theory to improve reasoning.
contribution: Provides theoretical justification through IB theory and demonstrates improved generalization through auxiliary latent-space computation via KV cache consolidation.

problem: Most scalable kernel methods assume stationarity, forcing a tradeoff between expressiveness (deep Gaussian processes) and efficiency (Random Fourier Features).
approach: Random Wavelet Features (RWF) constructs scalable non-stationary kernel approximations by sampling from wavelet families, leveraging their localization and multi-resolution structure.
contribution: Outperforms stationary random features on non-stationary datasets with convergence guarantees, offering compelling accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for real-world non-stationary problems.

problem: Metadata for LLM pretraining acceleration focuses only on URLs, leaving open questions about other metadata types and their positioning.
approach: Investigates multiple metadata types (fine-grained quality indicators) and positions (prepended and appended), with learnable meta-tokens trained via masked loss.
contribution: Identifies fine-grained metadata as effective accelerators and provides guidelines for metadata integration to improve efficiency and effectiveness of pretraining.

problem: Discovering insights from real-world data lakes requires orchestrating diverse data tasks (extraction, cleaning, integration, analysis), yet AI systems struggle with end-to-end pipelines.
approach: KramaBench features 104 manually curated challenges spanning 1,700 files across 6 domains and 24 data sources, with evaluation framework for pipeline design and task implementation.
contribution: Current single-agent systems reach only 50% end-to-end accuracy; even with perfect retrieval, accuracy tops at 59%, revealing challenges in pipeline orchestration.

problem: Direct reasoning over long, noisy documents is brittle; long-document QA requires consolidating dispersed evidence into verifiable structured outputs.
approach: LiteCoST uses Chain-of-Structured-Thought (CoST) with LLMs to produce traced reasoning and structured outputs, then fine-tunes SLMs in two phases: supervised training then Group Relative Policy Optimization.
contribution: Achieves LLM-comparable quality on finance and legal documents with 3B/7B SLMs while delivering 2-4× lower latency than GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1.

problem: Diffusion model inference is computationally expensive, and recent feature caching methods fail to model complex feature dynamics, suffering severe quality loss.
approach: HiCache uses Hermite polynomials to approximate feature derivatives (optimized for Gaussian-correlated processes) with dual-scaling for numerical stability.
contribution: Achieves 5.55× speedup on FLUX.1-dev while exceeding baseline quality, generalizes across text-to-image and video with 0.9480→0.9840 improvement when applied to existing methods.
